governance_posts.title: [ARFC] Permissioned GSM - USAT Aave V4 Avalanche
governance_posts.description:
title: [ARFC] Permissioned GSM - USAT Aave V4 Avalanche
author: @TokenLogic
created: 2026-10-15

Summary

TokenLogic proposes a Permissioned GHO Stability Module (GSM) that allows approved counterparties to exchange eligible assets for GHO and vice versa. The module would retain the existing GSM functionality while introducing participant-level access controls.

The first application would support USAT on Avalanche. Under this arrangement, USAT remains supplied to Aave V4 while the GSM holds waUSAT, the receipt token representing the supplied USAT. The proposal includes the funding and configuration needed to launch this instance.

Motivation

Existing GSMs allow users to exchange supported assets for GHO within governance-defined limits. However, some institutional arrangements require restricting access to approved counterparties, particularly when specific commercial terms or asset requirements apply.

A Permissioned GSM would support these arrangements without changing existing GSM exchange functionality.

Initial Application: USAT

USAT is a USD-backed stablecoin issued by Anchorage Digital Bank, N.A.

An approved counterparty would deposit USAT into the Aave V4 Tokenization Spoke and receive waUSAT. The counterparty would then separately exchange waUSAT for GHO through the Permissioned GSM, which would hold the waUSAT. Returning GHO would allow the counterparty to recover waUSAT. Redemption for underlying USAT would depend on the selected integration and available liquidity.

The same framework could support additional assets and counterparties. Multiple approved participants could share a GSM instance under the same configuration, while existing permissionless GSMs would remain unaffected.

Permissioned Access

Permissioning would apply to the swap originator in both directions. Approved participants could specify another recipient or use a relayer to submit a valid signed swap. Neither the recipient nor the relayer would require separate participant approval.

GHO received through the module would remain freely transferable. Revoking a participant’s approval would prevent further swaps, including exchanges intended to recover previously deposited assets.

Liquidity and Exposure Management

Each instance would operate with shared liquidity, allowing approved counterparties to exchange against the same pool under governance-defined limits. Liquidity would not be reserved for individual participants. The module would not track individual principal balances or require a participant’s swaps to match their previous deposits.

The reserve supplies the GHO needed for swaps. The Remote GSM Draw Limit caps the GSM’s use of that reserve. The Exposure Cap limits additional asset inflows through swaps. Exchange fees and any applicable accrued yield go to the configured treasury.

The exposure cap would be denominated in the configured asset, including share units where applicable. Exchanges would remain subject to sufficient available liquidity, independently of the configured limits.

Administration and Emergency Controls

Governance would assign configuration and emergency permissions.

The selected GSM implementation would retain its emergency controls, including the ability to freeze exchanges. Seizure transfers assets held by the module to the designated treasury and prevents further exchanges through the instance.

Revocation, freezing or insufficient liquidity could prevent counterparties from reversing an exchange. These restrictions would need to be reflected in the relevant counterparty agreements.

Specification

TokenLogic proposes deploying a permissioned remoteGSM on Avalanche to exchange waUSAT for GHO and vice versa.

Funding the GSM

A new GHO Reserve on Avalanche would provide GHO for the USAT GSM. We would bridge the initial allocation to the Avalanche Collector, which would then transfer the funds to the reserve. To support this transfer, we would increase the bridge limits and refill rates, then apply the ongoing settings once the transfer is complete, as we have done previously when deploying new GSMs on Plasma, Monad, and Arbitrum.

Access and Administration

title: [ARFC] Permissioned GSM - USAT Aave V4 Avalanche
author: @TokenLogic
created: 2026-10-15

Summary

TokenLogic proposes a Permissioned GHO Stability Module (GSM) that allows approved counterparties to exchange eligible assets for GHO and vice versa. The module would retain the existing GSM functionality while introducing participant-level access controls.

The first application would support USAT on Avalanche. Under this arrangement, USAT remains supplied to Aave V4 while the GSM holds waUSAT, the receipt token representing the supplied USAT. The proposal includes the funding and configuration needed to launch this instance.

Motivation

Existing GSMs allow users to exchange supported assets for GHO within governance-defined limits. However, some institutional arrangements require restricting access to approved counterparties, particularly when specific commercial terms or asset requirements apply.

A Permissioned GSM would support these arrangements without changing existing GSM exchange functionality.

Initial Application: USAT

USAT is a USD-backed stablecoin issued by Anchorage Digital Bank, N.A.

An approved counterparty would deposit USAT into the Aave V4 Tokenization Spoke and receive waUSAT. The counterparty would then separately exchange waUSAT for GHO through the Permissioned GSM, which would hold the waUSAT. Returning GHO would allow the counterparty to recover waUSAT. Redemption for underlying USAT would depend on the selected integration and available liquidity.

The same framework could support additional assets and counterparties. Multiple approved participants could share a GSM instance under the same configuration, while existing permissionless GSMs would remain unaffected.

Permissioned Access

Permissioning would apply to the swap originator in both directions. Approved participants could specify another recipient or use a relayer to submit a valid signed swap. Neither the recipient nor the relayer would require separate participant approval.

GHO received through the module would remain freely transferable. Revoking a participant’s approval would prevent further swaps, including exchanges intended to recover previously deposited assets.

Liquidity and Exposure Management

Each instance would operate with shared liquidity, allowing approved counterparties to exchange against the same pool under governance-defined limits. Liquidity would not be reserved for individual participants. The module would not track individual principal balances or require a participant’s swaps to match their previous deposits.

The reserve supplies the GHO needed for swaps. The Remote GSM Draw Limit caps the GSM’s use of that reserve. The Exposure Cap limits additional asset inflows through swaps. Exchange fees and any applicable accrued yield go to the configured treasury.

The exposure cap would be denominated in the configured asset, including share units where applicable. Exchanges would remain subject to sufficient available liquidity, independently of the configured limits.

Administration and Emergency Controls

Governance would assign configuration and emergency permissions.

The selected GSM implementation would retain its emergency controls, including the ability to freeze exchanges. Seizure transfers assets held by the module to the designated treasury and prevents further exchanges through the instance.

Revocation, freezing or insufficient liquidity could prevent counterparties from reversing an exchange. These restrictions would need to be reflected in the relevant counterparty agreements.

Specification

TokenLogic proposes deploying a permissioned remoteGSM on Avalanche to exchange waUSAT for GHO and vice versa.

Funding the GSM

A new GHO Reserve on Avalanche would provide GHO for the USAT GSM. We would bridge the initial allocation to the Avalanche Collector, which would then transfer the funds to the reserve. To support this transfer, we would increase the bridge limits and refill rates, then apply the ongoing settings once the transfer is complete, as we have done previously when deploying new GSMs on Plasma, Monad, and Arbitrum.

Access and Administration

The initial whitelist would include the commercial counterparty and an Aave DAO Safe, controlled by the Aave Finance Committee. Both would use the same shared liquidity and pricing, with GHO required to receive waUSAT. GHO Stewards would manage the exposure cap and swap fees within the proposed limits. The reserve limit manager would control the GSM’s GHO draw allowance through LIMIT_MANAGER_ROLE.

Only the GHO Stewards Safe (0x8513e6F37dBc52De87b166980Fa3F50639694B60) would be authorized to call the GHO GSM Steward’s parameter-update functions.

governance_posts.title: Risk Stewards: Supply and Borrow Cap Changes on Aave V3 / 2026.10.16
governance_posts.description:
Summary

LlamaRisk recommends the following parameter changes based on user behavior, position health, and borrow cap headroom observed in the latest review of Aave V3 reserves.

Aave V3 Prime:

  • Increase supply cap for tETH from 15,000 to 20,000.

Aave V3 Core:

  • Reduce supply cap for tETH from 300 to 1.
  • Reduce borrow cap for WBTC from 4,000 to 1,500.
  • Reduce borrow cap for cbBTC from 1,440 to 500.

Aave V3 Arbitrum:

  • Reduce borrow cap for WETH from 135,000 to 75,000.

tETH (Aave V3 Prime and Aave V3 Core)

tETH is listed on both Aave V3 Prime and Aave V3 Core, and on both instances, it counts as collateral only within E-Mode. On Aave V3 Prime, the reserve holds 15,189 tETH (approximately USD 46.9M) against a 15,000 supply cap (101.3% utilization). On Aave V3 Core, supply has remained between approximately 90 and 300 tETH since late April and stands at 286.78 tETH (approximately USD 0.9M), about 1.9% of the Prime figure.

Supply Distribution (Aave V3 Prime)


Source: LlamaRisk, October 16, 2026

The top tETH suppliers have health factors between 1.02 and 1.07 with a median of 1.05, all carry outstanding debt, and supply is highly concentrated, with the largest position accounting for 77.5% of the reserve. Every position borrows wstETH against tETH collateral within the tETH/wstETH E-Mode category, so the health factor of the cohort tracks the tETH/wstETH exchange rate.

Recommendation

Adoption of tETH on Aave V3 Core has remained low, while demand for the asset sits on Aave V3 Prime, where it is paired with wstETH debt in a dedicated E-Mode category. We recommend reducing the supply cap on Aave V3 Core from 300 to 1, which stops new deposits on that instance without affecting existing positions, and raising the supply cap on Aave V3 Prime from 15,000 to 20,000, which places the reserve at approximately 75.9% post-change cap utilization.

Borrow Cap Reductions

  • WBTC on Aave V3 Core carries 700 WBTC of debt (approximately USD 57.3M) against a 4,000 borrow cap (17.5% utilization), with borrows down 10.4% over the past 30 days. The proposed borrow cap of 1,500 lands at approximately 46.7% post-change borrow cap utilization, aligning the cap with observed demand while retaining headroom.
  • cbBTC on Aave V3 Core carries 128 cbBTC of debt (approximately USD 10.5M) against a 1,440 borrow cap (8.9% utilization), with borrows up 24.8% over the past seven days. The proposed borrow cap of 500 lands at approximately 25.7% post-change borrow cap utilization, retaining ample room for further growth.
  • WETH on Aave V3 Arbitrum carries 55,461 WETH of debt (approximately USD 136.0M) against a 135,000 borrow cap (41.1% utilization), with borrows broadly unchanged over the past 30 days. The proposed borrow cap of 75,000 lands at approximately 73.9% post-change borrow cap utilization, aligning the cap with observed demand.

Specification

Supply Caps

Instance Asset Current Supply Cap Recommended Supply Cap
Aave V3 Prime tETH 15,000 20,000
Aave V3 Core tETH 300 1

Borrow Caps

Instance Asset Current Borrow Cap Recommended Borrow Cap
Aave V3 Core WBTC 4,000 1,500
Aave V3 Core cbBTC 1,440 500
Aave V3 Arbitrum WETH 135,000 75,000

Next Steps

We will move forward and implement these updates via the Risk Steward process. The implemented changes can be reviewed on the LlamaRisk Risk Stewards Dashboard.

Summary

This proposal seeks to onboard USAT to the Aave V4 Core Instance on Avalanche. This proposal follows the Direct to AIP route.

Motivation

USAT (Tether America USD) is a dollar stablecoin issued by Anchorage Digital Bank, N.A., a federally chartered national trust bank supervised by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC). USAT is subject to the GENIUS Act and is redeemable 1:1 for U.S. dollars.

Onboarding USAT would:

  • Add a stablecoin issued by a bank under federal supervision in the United States to the Aave V4 Core Instance on Avalanche.
  • Support demand from institutional participants seeking a stablecoin issued under the federal stablecoin framework of the United States.
  • Broaden the range of regulated dollar assets available across Aave deployments.

Summary

LlamaRisk recommends the following parameter changes based on user behavior, on-chain liquidity, and position health observed in the latest review of Aave V3 reserves.

Aave V3 Core:

  • WPOL on Aave V3 Polygon sits at 49.5% supply cap utilization, with supply down 34.2% over the past seven days. The proposed supply cap of 65M is approximately 1.30x current outstanding supply, landing at approximately 76.9% post-change cap utilization. governance_posts.title: [Direct-to-AIP] Asset Listing - syrupUSDC X Layer
governance_posts.description:
title: [Direct-to-AIP] Asset Listing - syrupUSDC X Layer
author: @TokenLogic
created: 2026-10-20

Summary

This publication proposes onboarding syrupUSDC to Aave V3 X Layer. It would be collateral only within a new E-Mode for borrowing stablecoins, and not collateral outside that E-Mode. Input from the Risk and Technical Service Providers is requested.

Motivation

syrupUSDC

syrupUSDC is Maple Finance’s yield-bearing USDC token. Users deposit USDC into Maple’s Syrup pool on Ethereum and receive syrupUSDC. Maple lends the pooled USDC to institutional borrowers through overcollateralized loans. Interest accrues to the token’s exchange rate against USDC.

The token is an ERC-4626 vault on Ethereum. Chainlink CCIP bridges it to Solana, Monad, Arc, Base and Arbitrum, among other chains: syrupUSDC is locked on Ethereum and minted on the destination chain.

syrupUSDC is already listed on Aave V3 Monad and Aave V3 Base, as collateral within a syrupUSDC / Stablecoins E-Mode, and on Aave V4 Arc, on the Maple SyrupUSDC spoke of the Core Hub.

Supply and Adoption

As of 16 Oct 2026, syrupUSDC has 889.7M tokens outstanding (about $1.06B at the current exchange rate) across six chains.

Supply grew from about 60M in March 2025 to over 1B by October 2025, and peaked at 1.66B in March 2026. It has since settled at 0.8–0.9B. Since mid-2026, new supply has come mainly from Monad, where syrupUSDC grew from launch in May 2026 to 136.1M, and from Arc, live since September 2026.

Yield Profile

syrupUSDC has accrued yield since June 2024. Over the past 12 months, its trailing 30-day APY eased from 6.8% in October 2025 to a low of 4.3% in April 2026. Since then it has stayed in a narrow ~4.4%–5.2% range, and it now stands at 5.1%.

Over the past three months, daily APY has a mean of 5.02%, a median of 4.98% and a standard deviation of 0.22pp.

The yield is predictable and stable, which makes syrupUSDC a good fit for a stablecoin carry trade on Aave. Users can post syrupUSDC in the E-Mode and borrow stablecoins while the borrow rate stays below syrupUSDC’s yield. That creates sustained borrowing demand for X Layer’s stablecoin reserves.

Loan Book and Collateral

The syrupUSDC pool lends USDC to institutional borrowers through overcollateralized loans. As of 16 Oct 2026, it has $1,036M of loans outstanding:

  • BTC-backed: $797.8M (20 loans)
  • XRP-backed: $96.6M (2 loans)
  • ETH-backed: $50.8M (3 loans)
  • T-Bills (Superstate USTB and PYUSD): $71.0M
  • AMM: $20.0M

These loans are backed by $1,749M of collateral, 78% of it BTC.

The BTC-, ETH- and XRP-backed loans total $945.2M of principal, secured by $1,657.8M of collateral. That is an average collateralization level of about 175%. Over half of that principal sits at a collateralization level of 190% or more; 29% ($277M) sits between 119% and 150%.

Value Proposition

syrupUSDC’s 30-day APY is ~5.1%, above the borrow rates of X Layer’s main stablecoin markets. Users can loop that spread into a leveraged carry position.

This listing creates stable, sticky borrowing demand for X Layer’s stablecoin reserves, which increases utilization and supply rates and attracts additional stablecoin deposits.

Maple has also committed to seeding $2M in syrupUSDC liquidity on X Layer. Local liquidity makes it easier for borrowers to enter and exit positions and enables liquidators to close positions without bridge delays, supporting the market from launch.

Specification

Asset Details

Proposed Market Configuration

We propose the following initial configuration for syrupUSDC, subject to final recommendations from Aave’s Risk Service Providers.

E-Mode Configuration

E-Mode: syrupUSDC / Stablecoins

Oracle

syrupUSDC would be priced through a Dynamic CAPO adapter. The adapter takes the syrupUSDC/USDC exchange rate and multiplies it by a capped USDC/USD price.

The adapter has two components:

USDC/USD price

A Chainlink USDC/USD feed is live on X Layer at 0xB8a08c178D96C315FbFB5661ABD208477391BC40. Aave V3 X Layer already uses it for the USDC reserve, through the Capped USDC/USD adapter 0x26ad1207eaa39f74fac725599ce1c431c80ef6cc with a 1.04 price cap. We propose reusing that adapter as the base price feed.

syrupUSDC/USDC exchange rate

A Chainlink syrupUSDC/USDC Exchange Rate feed is live on X Layer at 0x04c00259887Cc94764DF190c8D3663c765618204. It relays the exchange rate from the syrupUSDC vault on Ethereum.

The CAPO parameters will be set by the Risk Service Providers. The final oracle contracts and configuration remain subject to confirmation by Aave’s Risk and Technical Service Providers.

Disclaimer

TokenLogic is an active service provider to the Aave DAO, the beneficiary of stream 100086 and the KPI as outlined in this publication. The scope of this engagement is available via this forum proposal.

TokenLogic supports and maintains an independent delegate voting platform within the Aave community.

TokenLogic and associated entities have no undisclosed material conflicts of interest at the time of submission.

Next Steps

  1. Gather feedback from the community.
  2. Using the Direct-to-AIP process, incorporate feedback from the Risk Service Provider and the Technical Service Provider.
  3. Confirm the following are deployed on X Layer:
    • syrupUSDC, with X Layer added to the Chainlink CCIP lane
    • syrupUSDC liquidity seeded on a DEX
  4. Deposit at least $150 worth of syrupUSDC into the Aave Short Executor on X Layer before the market goes live, as required by Aave Governance Framework v2.
  5. Escalate to the AIP Voting stage.

Copyright

Copyright and related rights waived via CC0.

governance_posts.title: [ARFC] Aave V3.8
governance_posts.description:
Summary

This proposal seeks to upgrade Aave V3 to V3.8, a non-invasive and very measured release focused on security. The changes it introduces are quite minor, but we consider them worth applying to make the system more robust and resilient going forward.

It includes the following changes:

  • A reentrancy guard on Pool operations during external callbacks.

Securing Aave V3 remains a top priority, and additional security reviews are being planned. Further defense-in-depth improvements may be proposed in future upgrades.

Motivation

Aave V3.8 aims to make the system more robust and predictable. Gas costs are no longer the concern they once were, and recent developments such as transient storage allow the protocol to be strengthened with little downside in efficiency or gas costs.

Aave V3.8 Changes

1. Reentrancy hardening

Aave V3.8 introduces a guard based on transient storage (EIP-1153) that protects Pool accounting consistency, including when a single transaction’s execution flow interacts with the Pool more than once. The change is intended to strengthen the robustness and security of the protocol over the long term, aligning the pools with industry best practice and protecting them against theoretical reentrancy exploits. Gas costs were historically a concern for this type of guard. With transient storage, that concern is no longer valid, as the guard can be applied with little overhead.

Deployment Rollout Plan

The upgrade targets the Aave V3 instances on Ethereum (Core and Lido), Plasma, Avalanche, BNB, Monad, Base, Arbitrum, Mantle, X Layer, Polygon, Linea, Optimism, Gnosis, MegaETH, and Celo. Only active instances are in scope. Instances, where all assets are frozen and caps are being set to zero, are not included.

Licensing

Aave V3.8 will be published as its own version of the Licensed Work under a Business Source License. The licence text is available here and will be included in the V3.8 repository. The Change Date for V3.8 is set by Aave Governance and recorded in the change-date text record at v38.aavelicense.eth. Until Governance sets a date, V3.8 stays under the Business Source License. As with the other codebase IP, the V3.8 IP will be transferred to the Aave Foundation through a separate governance proposal.

Security procedures

Aave V3.8 will go through a round of audits by Certora and third parties before AIP.

Disclaimer

Aave Labs is presenting this proposal as a contributor to the Aave ecosystem, as part of its ongoing work on the Aave Protocol, and has no undisclosed financial interest in its outcome.

Next Steps

  1. Gather community feedback during the ARFC stage.
  2. If the ARFC response is positive, escalate to Snapshot for offchain confirmation.
  3. Upon completion of the audits, submit an AIP to Aave Governance to upgrade the Aave V3 instances in scope to V3.8.

title: [Direct-To-AIP] Onboard PT-sUSDe-28JAN2027 to Aave V3 Plasma Instance

author: @TokenLogic

created: 2026-10-21

Summary

This proposal seeks to list PT-sUSDe-28JAN2027 on Aave V3 Plasma through the Direct-to-AIP process, providing a rollover destination for users of PT-sUSDe-22OCT2026 ahead of its maturity on 22 October 2026.

Motivation

PT-sUSDe-22OCT2026 matures on 22 October 2026, with approximately 20.72M PT supplied to Aave V3 Plasma as of 21 October. The proposed January listing would allow holders to roll into the next maturity and continue using PT-sUSDe as collateral on the instance.

The rollover follows the established sequence of sUSDe PT listings on Plasma, covering the January, April, June and October 2026 maturities.

At the time of writing, the January PT has approximately 99 days remaining until maturity, compared with approximately 132 days when the October PT was assessed. The shorter remaining term reduces the PT’s price sensitivity to changes in implied yield, supporting the case for risk parameters at least in line with the October listing, subject to Risk Service Providers’ assessment of liquidity and liquidation conditions.

governance_posts.title: Risk Stewards: Cap and IRM Changes on Aave V3 / 2026.10.23
governance_posts.description:
Summary

LlamaRisk recommends the following parameter changes based on user behavior, on-chain liquidity, and position health observed in the latest review of Aave V3 reserves.

Aave V3 Core:

  • Reduce supply cap for cbBTC from 22,800 to 20,000.
  • Reduce supply cap for sUSDe from 130,000,000 to 105,000,000.
  • Reduce supply cap for USDe from 300,000,000 to 275,000,000.
  • Reduce supply cap for PT-srUSDe-22OCT2026 from 20,000,000 to 1.

Aave V3 Plasma:

  • Reduce supply cap for PT-sUSDE-22OCT2026 from 50,000,000 to 1.

Aave V3 Avalanche:

  • Reduce supply cap for WAVAX from 18,160,000 to 16,000,000.

Aave V3 Arbitrum:

  • Increase Slope1 for USDC from 4.00% to 4.10%.

Aave V3 X Layer:

  • Reduce supply cap for PT-USDG-29OCT2026 from 140,000,000 to 50,000,000.
  • Reduce supply cap for xETH from 20,000 to 10,000.
  • Reduce borrow cap for xETH from 8,080 to 5,000.
  • Reduce supply cap for xBTC from 500 to 200.
  • Reduce supply cap for xBETH from 11,400 to 5,000.
  • Reduce supply cap for xOKSOL from 135,000 to 75,000.

USDC Slope1 Increase (Aave V3 Arbitrum)

USDC on Aave V3 Arbitrum holds approximately 218.2M USDC of supply against 170.5M of debt, at 78.1% utilization against a 90% optimal utilization point. Over the past 30 days, supply grew 30.1% while debt grew 9.4%, bringing utilization down from 92.7%.


Source: USDC V3 Arbitrum Utilization, LlamaRisk, October 23, 2026

The recommendation raises Slope1 by 10 BPS, from 4.00% to 4.10%. The base rate, Slope2, and the optimal utilization point are unchanged, so the borrow rate at the optimal point moves from 4.00% to 4.10% APR and the rate at full utilization from 14.00% to 14.10% APR.

Instance Asset Utilization uOptimal Current Borrow APR New Borrow APR Delta
Aave V3 Arbitrum USDC 78.1% 90.0% 3.47% 3.56% +9 BPS

USDC on Aave V3 Arbitrum carries a lower Slope1 than the 4.50% applied to most stablecoin reserves across Aave V3, including USD₮0 on the same instance. We plan to raise Slope1 toward 4.50% gradually, in incremental steps, with the size and timing of each step set by observed borrow demand, utilization, and broader market conditions.

Cap Reductions

  • cbBTC on Aave V3 Core sits at 76.2% supply cap utilization (17,376 / 22,800), with supply down 4.8% over the past 30 days. The proposed cap of 20,000 is approximately 1.15x current outstanding supply, landing at approximately 86.9% post-change cap utilization.
  • sUSDe on Aave V3 Core sits at 80.0% supply cap utilization (104,041,171 / 130,000,000), with supply down 33.8% over the past 30 days. The proposed cap of 105,000,000 is approximately 1.01x current outstanding supply, landing at approximately 99.1% post-change cap utilization.
  • USDe on Aave V3 Core sits at 85.3% supply cap utilization (255,895,303 / 300,000,000), with supply down 58.2% over the past 30 days. The proposed cap of 275,000,000 is approximately 1.07x current outstanding supply, landing at approximately 93.1% post-change cap utilization.
  • WAVAX on Aave V3 Avalanche sits at 92.3% supply cap utilization (16,758,718 / 18,160,000), with supply down 3.7% over the past 30 days. The proposed cap of 16,000,000 sits below current outstanding supply (approximately 104.7% post-change cap utilization).
  • PT-USDG-29OCT2026 on Aave V3 X Layer sits at 27.6% supply cap utilization (38,635,925 / 140,000,000), with supply down 46.0% over the past 30 days ahead of its October 29, 2026 maturity. The proposed cap of 50,000,000 is approximately 1.29x current outstanding supply, landing at approximately 77.3% post-change cap utilization.
  • xETH on Aave V3 X Layer sits at 32.9% supply cap utilization (6,579 / 20,000), with supply down 11.6% over the past 30 days. The proposed supply cap of 10,000 is approximately 1.52x current outstanding supply, landing at approximately 65.8% post-change cap utilization. The reserve carries 1,464 xETH of debt against an 8,080 borrow cap (18.1% utilization), with borrows down 51.2% over the past 30 days, and the proposed borrow cap of 5,000 lands at approximately 29.3% post-change borrow cap utilization.
  • xBTC on Aave V3 X Layer sits at 16.4% supply cap utilization (81.8 / 500), with supply down 13.1% over the past 30 days. The proposed cap of 200 is approximately 2.45x current outstanding supply, landing at approximately 40.9% post-change cap utilization.
  • xBETH on Aave V3 X Layer sits at 13.9% supply cap utilization (1,589 / 11,400), with supply down 42.8% over the past 30 days. The proposed cap of 5,000 is approximately 3.15x current outstanding supply, landing at approximately 31.8% post-change cap utilization.
  • xOKSOL on Aave V3 X Layer sits below 0.1% supply cap utilization (13.8 / 135,000), with supply down 94.3% over the past 30 days. The proposed cap of 75,000 keeps post-change cap utilization below 0.1%.

Matured PTs

  • PT-srUSDe-22OCT2026 on Aave V3 Core reached its scheduled maturity on October 22, 2026. The reserve holds approximately 601,419 PT against a 20,000,000 supply cap, with supply down 80.0% over the past 30 days ahead of maturity. After maturity, the PT becomes redeemable at par against the underlying. The proposed supply cap of 1 closes new deposits while existing holders retain the ability to withdraw or redeem.
  • PT-sUSDE-22OCT2026 on Aave V3 Plasma reached its scheduled maturity on October 22, 2026. The reserve holds approximately 1,568,767 PT against a 50,000,000 supply cap, with supply down 97.4% over the past 30 days ahead of maturity. We recommend lowering its supply cap to 1 too to close new deposits.

governance_posts.title: Risk Stewards: Cap and IRM Changes on Aave V4 / 2026.10.23
governance_posts.description:
Summary

LlamaRisk recommends the following parameter changes based on user behavior, on-chain liquidity, and position health observed in the latest review of Aave V4 reserves.

Aave V4 Ethereum:

  • Increase slope1 for USDC and USDT on the Plus Hub from 4.60% to 4.70%.
  • Increase the add cap for USDT on the Prime Hub Bluechip Spoke from 13.125M to 20M.
  • Increase the draw cap for USDT on the Prime Hub Bluechip Spoke from 15.625M to 18.4M.
  • Decrease the draw cap for USDG on the Global Dollar Hub PAXG Gold Spoke from 9.5M to 5M.
  • Increase the add cap for USDG on the Global Dollar Hub USDG Maple Spoke from 55M to 65M.
  • Increase the draw cap for USDG on the Global Dollar Hub USDG Maple Spoke from 50M to 60M.
  • Increase the add cap for syrupUSDG on the Global Dollar Hub USDG Maple Spoke from 70M to 75M.
  • Decrease the draw cap for USDG on the Global Dollar Hub USDG Pendle Spoke from 4M to 0.
  • Decrease the draw cap for USDG on the Core Hub USDG Pendle Spoke from 15M to 0.

Aave V4 Avalanche:

  • Increase the add cap for WAVAX on the Core Hub Main Spoke from 1M to 2M.

USDC and USDT IRM (Plus Hub)

USDC and USDT on the Plus Hub have supplies of 3.00M and 3.03M, with utilization rates of 89.2% and 91.7%, respectively. The Plus Hub applies a 15% liquidity fee, compared with 10% on the Core and Prime Hubs, so at the current slope1 of 4.60%, the supply rate on the Plus Hub sits below most comparable passive stablecoin supply yields on Ethereum.

Venue USDC Supply APY USDT Supply APY
Aave V3 Core (30-day average) 4.17% 3.86%
Aave V4 Core Hub (October median) 4.33% 3.54%
Aave V4 Prime Hub (October median) 4.13% 3.73%
Aave V4 Plus Hub, current 3.44% 3.64%
Aave V4 Plus Hub, proposed 3.51% 3.72%

At current utilization, the proposed slope1 of 4.70% raises the Plus Hub supply APY by 0.07 percentage points for USDC and 0.08 percentage points for USDT, and to 3.74% at the optimal point.

On the borrow side, the USDC rate at current utilization moves from 4.46% to 4.55% and the USDT rate from 4.58% to 4.68%. The optimal usage ratio (92.00%), base rate (0.00%), and slope2 (20.00%) remain unchanged.


Source: LlamaRisk, October 23, 2026

Recommendation

We recommend increasing slope1 for USDC and USDT on the Plus Hub from 4.60% to 4.70%, which makes the Plus Hub supply rate more attractive to depositors. Ethena incentives are live at a 5.5% target APR, which keeps USDe stablecoin loops profitable at the proposed borrow rates while retaining a spread slightly better than on the Aave V3 Core market.

USDT (Prime Hub)

USDT on the Prime Hub holds 2.98M added and 2.53M drawn, for a hub utilization of 84.8% against an optimal usage ratio of 92.00%. The Bluechip Spoke accounts for all USDT drawn on the Prime Hub.

Recommendation

The proposed caps raise the USDT add cap on the Bluechip Spoke to 20M and the draw cap to 18.4M, creating headroom for larger USDT deposits and the borrowing they support on the Prime Hub. governance_posts.title: Aave DeFi Watcher – Browser Extension for Monitoring Aave Positions
governance_posts.description:
Hi dear aave community :)

I’d like to share Aave DeFi Watcher, a browser extension I built to make monitoring Aave positions simple, fast, and privacy-friendly.

I originally started building it because the previously shared Aave Monitor extension appears to no longer function reliably. For example, many addresses currently return “Failed to fetch” instead of account data. It also only supports Aave V3, while I wanted a tool that could monitor positions across Aave V2, V3, and V4. Since I needed a working solution myself, I decided to build one from scratch.

Features

  • Total Collateral
  • Total Debt
  • Available to Borrow
  • Loan-to-Value (LTV)
  • Liquidation Threshold
  • Health Factor
  • Monitor multiple wallet addresses
  • Support for Aave V2, V3, and V4
  • Support for multiple networks including Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Polygon, and Avalanche
  • Desktop notifications for Health Factor alerts
  • Privacy Mode to hide balances while continuing to monitor your positions
  • Automatic RPC fallback for improved reliability

One of my favorite features is the extension badge, which displays the Health Factor of your selected address directly on the browser toolbar, allowing you to monitor your position at a glance.

The extension is completely read-only. It never asks you to connect a wallet or sign transactions. All account data is fetched directly from Aave’s public smart contracts.

Chrome Web Store

chromewebstore.google.com

Aave DeFi Watcher - Chrome Web Store

Monitor your Aave health factor and liquidation risk in real time across chains.

I built this extension for my own daily use and decided to share it with the community. It’s actively maintained, and I plan to continue adding new features and supporting future Aave releases.

I’d really appreciate any feedback, bug reports or feature suggestions from the community :))

governance_posts.title: Question regarding Acier's alleged misrepresentation and deception of investors
governance_posts.description:
Acier is a new lending and borrowing protocol founded by @MarcZeller (ACI) and @eboado (BGD Labs), both former core contributors to Aave.

As a former ACI employee and a current Acier investor, I am raising several questions about Acier’s alleged misleading and deceptive conduct towards investors.

I have included a direct quote from @eboado . If a founder can treat his investors disrespectfully and unreasonably, he is even less likely to treat his users with respect and sincerity.

I urge everyone not to use his platform in the future.

First, the pitch deck used for public fundraising presents ACI and BGD as the two core teams behind Acier. I am a former ACI employee, an Acier investor, a former co-founder of the Paper Tiger project alongside Marc Zeller, and Marc’s friend and neighbour. Throughout my communications with Marc Zeller, I was led to believe that he was the person leading Acier. However, I cannot entirely rule out the possibility that this was my own subjective misperception. Nevertheless, Acier’s ownership structure was never explicitly disclosed in any of the public materials available to me. It was not until October 1, after my repeated questions, that Marc clarified that he owned one-third of Acier and BGD owned two-thirds.

Second, I question the continued existence of ACI, one of the two entities presented as making up Acier. Apart from Marc Zeller, the ACI team previously included Togbe, Cris, Xavi, Martin, Nandy, Alice and myself. Now, only Marc Zeller remains. I therefore personally question whether ACI still exists as a team. As to whether ACI continues to exist as a legal entity, I ask Marc Zeller to provide a clear answer.

Based on my own observations and knowledge of both teams, my personal inference is that ACI is responsible for business development, corresponding to its previous role in the Aave ecosystem, while BGD is responsible for technology. However, Mark Agranovski, who currently handles business development for Acier, uses a BGD email address rather than an ACI email address. I also personally suspect an element of cronyism here, given his connection to Ernesto as a salesperson who previously sold him AT1 bonds. Ernesto did not deny this in our communications. If ACI still exists as a legal entity, why is this person not employed by ACI? I ask Marc and Ernesto to explain the specific division of responsibilities between ACI and BGD within Acier.

Having raised these concerns, on October 22, I asked Ernesto for Acier’s external promotional materials as an investor. I only had photographs of one document and was concerned that they might be incomplete, potentially causing misunderstandings. Ernesto answered: “ Once again, we have been communicating with Echo (including yesterday during /after discussing with you) on how to proceed with your replacing, and they compromised to come back to us as soon as possible. They are consulting (their legal and engineering team) on how to proceed. We have also told them that we can cover any additional cost on their side in order to make the process faster for you to be happy with the outcome. Now it seems that you are not really reasonable even with us telling you we are doing the best of our efforts on a situation that depends more on Echo (the entity you invested through) than on us and you have some type of ill intentions towards Acier, claiming very serious accusations like that we mislead our investors. Because of that, you should reach your contact on Echo ( Marc, and he can also connect you with the Echo team), and I will stop as of now any communication with you” I consider this conduct a blatant denial of my right to information as an investor.

For the first two reasons outlined above, I clearly stated my position to Marc and Ernesto on October 1: I had invested in the Acier led by Marc Zeller, not the Acier led by BGD, and I therefore requested the return of my investment. They both agreed to my request and did actively contacted Echo to move the relevant process forward. I also made it clear that I do not want any further involvement with Acier thus I want my investment returned as soon as possible; thus I proposed other solutions as well, but they have insisted on their own solution and procedures without providing any firm commitment or timeline.

If any part of the account above is inaccurate, we can each provide evidence to substantiate our respective accounts.

governance_posts.title: [Direct to AIP] Whitelist New CoW Protocol Adapters as Flash Borrowers on Aave V3/V4
governance_posts.description:
Title: [Direct to AIP] Whitelist New CoW Protocol Adapters as Flash Borrowers on Aave V3/V4
Author: @AaveLabs
Date: 2026-10-28

Summary

This proposal seeks to register the new Aave Swap Adapter factories as approved flash borrowers across relevant Aave V3 instances, enabling them to access flash liquidity with zero flash loan fees. The new factories serve the collateral swap, debt swap, repay with collateral, and leverage adapters.

This change improves execution quality for users interacting through Aave’s swap and leverage flows by removing an internal protocol fee that currently adds avoidable cost to adapter-based routing.

Motivation

Aave swap adapters support collateral swaps, debt swaps, repayments with collateral, and leverage inside the Aave experience. When a route requires flash liquidity, the flash loan premium is embedded directly in execution. That reduces output on collateral and debt swaps, increases the cost of opening leveraged positions, and prolongs the payback period of debt swaps, which weakens the Aave route against external alternatives.

Whitelisting the new CoW Swap Adapter factories removes that cost across the covered Aave V3 instances, and extends it to the new leverage adapter. CoW Swap Adapter routes that rely on flash liquidity will execute without a flash loan fee. Users will experience improved collateral swap, debt swap, and leverage pricing on Aave V3. With better pricing, the Aave interface should retain more of this flow within the Aave experience. Under the Aave Will Win Framework, the DAO is positioned to capture all revenue from that activity.

Specification

The Aave DAO would authorize the registration of the new Aave swap adapter factory contracts as approved flash borrowers through the ACLManager.addFlashBorrower function on the applicable Aave V3 deployments.

Once registered, these factories would be exempt from flash loan fees when using flash liquidity through the approved path.

The proposal payload would:

  • identify the swap adapter factory contract addresses to be registered
  • call addFlashBorrower for each factory on the relevant markets

CoW Swap Adapter Factories

Two factory versions are in scope, AaveV3AdapterV3Factory and AaveV3AdapterV4Factory. Each serves its own set of CollateralSwap, DebtSwap, RepayWithCollateral, and Leverage adapters.

Aave V3 instances included in scope

The payload will register the following factories as approved flash borrowers on the following Aave V3 instances:

governance_posts.description:
Summary

LlamaRisk recommends the following parameter changes based on user behavior, on-chain liquidity, and position health observed in the latest review of Aave V3 reserves.

Aave V3 Core:

  • Increase optimalUsageRatio for USDT from 92.00% to 94.00%.

Aave V3 Base:

  • Increase supply cap for cbETH from 60,000 to 70,000.

Aave V3 Avalanche:

  • Reduce supply cap for WAVAX from 16,000,000 to 14,000,000.

Aave V3 Arbitrum:

  • Increase Slope1 for USDC from 4.10% to 4.20%.

Aave V3 X Layer:

  • Reduce supply cap for PT-USDG-29OCT2026 from 50,000,000 to 1.
  • Reduce supply cap for USDe from 100,000,000 to 25,000,000.
  • Reduce borrow cap for USDe from 20,000,000 to 10,000,000.

cbETH (Aave V3 Base)

cbETH has reached 94.0% supply cap utilization (56,378 / 60,000) on the Aave V3 Base instance, with supply up 22.3% over the past 30 days.

cbETH Supply Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, October 29, 2026

All of the top twenty cbETH suppliers carry debt, at health factors between 1.02 and 15.30 with a median of 1.18, and supply is concentrated, with the largest supplier holding approximately 34% and the top three approximately 77%. Eleven borrow WETH against cbETH, which accounts for nearly all of the cohort’s debt, and ten hold smaller USDC borrowings, so HF for most of the debt depends on the cbETH-versus-ETH spread.

Recommendation

We recommend raising the supply cap from 60,000 to 70,000 on Aave V3 Base, landing at approximately 80.5% post-change cap utilization.

Cap Reductions

  • WAVAX on Aave V3 Avalanche sits at 101.9% supply cap utilization (16,298,323 / 16,000,000), with supply down 7.3% over the past 30 days. The proposed cap of 14,000,000 sits below current outstanding supply (approximately 116.4% post-change cap utilization), which limits further growth in WAVAX collateral while DEX liquidity for WAVAX on Avalanche remains limited.
  • USDe on Aave V3 X Layer sits at 2.7% supply cap utilization (2,746,676 / 100,000,000) with no outstanding debt against a 20,000,000 borrow cap. The proposed supply cap of 25,000,000 is approximately 9.1x current outstanding supply, landing at approximately 11.0% post-change cap utilization, and the borrow cap moves from 20,000,000 to 10,000,000.

Matured PTs

  • PT-USDG-29OCT2026 on Aave V3 X Layer reached its scheduled maturity on October 29, 2026. The reserve holds approximately 5,591,013 PT against a 50,000,000 supply cap, with supply down 91.6% over the past 30 days ahead of maturity. After maturity, the PT becomes redeemable at par against the underlying. The proposed supply cap of 1 closes new deposits while existing holders retain the ability to withdraw or redeem.

USDC Slope1 Increase (Aave V3 Arbitrum)

USDC on Aave V3 Arbitrum holds approximately 218.8M USDC of supply against 168.3M of debt, at 76.9% utilization against a 90% optimal utilization point. Over the past 30 days, supply grew 21.4% while debt grew 6.4%, bringing utilization down from 87.8%.

The recommendation raises Slope1 by 10 BPS, from 4.10% to 4.20%. The base rate, Slope2, and the optimal utilization point are unchanged, so the borrow rate at the optimal point moves from 4.10% to 4.20% APR and the rate at full utilization from 14.10% to 14.20% APR.

Instance Asset Utilization uOptimal Current Borrow APR New Borrow APR Delta
Aave V3 Arbitrum USDC 76.9% 90.0% 3.50% 3.59% +9 BPS

USDC on Aave V3 Arbitrum carries a lower Slope1 than the 4.50% applied to most stablecoin reserves across Aave V3, including USD₮0 on the same instance. We plan to continue raising Slope1 toward 4.50% gradually, in incremental steps, with the size and timing of each step set by observed borrow demand, utilization, and broader market conditions.

USDT Optimal Utilization (Aave V3 Core)

USDT on Aave V3 Core holds approximately 2.7B USDT of supply against 2.5B of debt, at 92.9% utilization, above the current 92.00% optimal point. The blue-chip collateral LTV increase on Aave V3 Core (WETH, WBTC, cbBTC, wstETH and weETH) executed on October 28, 2026, and the recommendation returns the optimal utilization point to 94.00%. The base rate, Slope1, and Slope2 are unchanged, so the borrow rate at the optimal point stays at 4.50% APR and the rate at full utilization stays at 14.50% APR.

At the current 92.9% utilization, the reserve moves from the Slope2 segment back onto Slope1: the variable borrow rate would move from 5.56% to 4.45% APR, and the supply rate from 4.65% to 3.71% APR.

governance_posts.description:
Summary

Following the freeze of Aave V3 and Aave V4 reserves in response to the Binance hot wallet incident on October 29, 2026, LlamaRisk recommends temporarily reducing Slope2 for stablecoin reserves, and for WETH on the Aave V4 Ethereum Core Hub, so that the variable borrow rate at full utilization does not exceed 10.00% APR. The base rate, Slope1 and optimal utilization point are unchanged, so borrow rates at or below the optimal point are unaffected. The changes apply to reserves with more than $10M supplied, utilization above or within 5 percentage points of the optimal point, and a borrow rate at full utilization above 10.00% APR, together with GHO on Aave V3 Monad.

Aave V4 Arc:

Rationale

Frozen reserves accept no new supply or borrowing, while withdrawals, repayments and liquidations continue to function. Since the freeze, supplier withdrawals have pushed the largest stablecoin reserves across Aave V3 and Aave V4 to between 92% and 100% utilization, where current Slope2 settings put variable borrow rates between 10% and 36% APR, and up to 55% APR at full utilization on some reserves. With new supply blocked, a rate above the optimal point no longer attracts deposits, and borrowers cannot add collateral to frozen reserves, so the elevated rate mostly accrues to borrower debt and erodes health factors while the freeze lasts.

The rate at full utilization equals the sum of the base rate, Slope1 and Slope2, so each reserve’s target Slope2 is 10.00% minus its base rate and Slope1. The changes are a temporary measure for the freeze period, and we will review the previous Slope2 settings as reserves are unfrozen.

Aave V3 Horizon was not frozen, but supplier withdrawals have pushed RLUSD to 94.1% utilization, where the borrow rate stands at 15.2% APR and reaches 30.0% APR at full utilization. We apply the same 10.00% cap to RLUSD on Horizon for consistency across Aave during the incident. governance_posts.title: Binance Hot Wallet Exploit: Aave's Response
governance_posts.description:
Last updated 01:00 UTC, 30 October 2026.

What happened

At 20:24 UTC on 29 October 2026, a Binance hot wallet on Ethereum sent about 63 tokens and 167,464 ETH to a single address in one transaction. The same exploiter address received a further 28,006 ETH from a second Binance hot wallet on Ethereum, and funds on Arbitrum, Optimism and Avalanche within the following minutes. A second inflow of 444,537 AVAX on Avalanche at 23:04 UTC suggests the compromise was still active more than two hours later.

The exploiter has since spread the funds across more than 20 new wallets and is selling tokens such as UNI, LINK and AAVE for ETH on decentralised exchanges.

Between 20:58 and 21:01 UTC, one wallet in the exploiter’s cluster supplied 60M USDT on Aave V3 Ethereum Core and borrowed 19,762 WETH, worth about $44.6M at the time. This happened about 40 minutes before the first freeze at 21:42, and no exploiter wallet has interacted with Aave since 21:01. It is the exploiter’s only position on Aave across all networks and versions. The position holds $59.9M of USDT collateral against $43.8M of debt, so it is over-collateralised and remains subject to normal liquidation. It does not put Aave suppliers at risk.

What we did

Within 10 minutes of the first reports we joined Aave Labs, TokenLogic, and Certora in a joint war room. The group decided to freeze Aave markets across all networks. The exploiter could swap the stolen funds into any listed asset, so freezing only the stolen token reserves would have left other ways in. We chose a freeze because the guardian can reverse it, while cutting caps instead would have needed a governance vote and about five days to restore.

A freeze stops anyone, including the exploiter, from opening new supply or borrow positions. Users can still repay and withdraw, and liquidations keep running. Because frozen reserves take no new supply, users cannot add collateral, so while the freeze is on, repaying is the only way to raise a health factor.

Together with Aave Labs’ engineering team, we prepared and simulated the freeze transactions for every network and proposed them to the guardian multisigs, which signed and executed them between 21:42 and 23:04 UTC. In total, 175 reserves were frozen on Aave V3 across 16 networks and 117 on Aave V4 across four networks. The freeze now covers:

  • Aave V3 on the Ethereum Core and Prime markets and on Arbitrum, Avalanche, Base, BNB Chain, Celo, Gnosis, Ink, Linea, Mantle, MegaETH, Monad, Optimism, Plasma, Polygon and X Layer.
  • Aave V4 on the main Ethereum spokes, the Avalanche spokes, the Base tokenized equities spoke and the Arc spokes.

The Horizon RWA market was left open because all of its collateral is permissioned and cannot be used by the exploiter. No market has been paused.

We also track the exploiter in real time. We follow every wallet in its cluster on Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism and Avalanche, watch for any interaction with Aave, and monitor the Chainlink price feeds that Aave relies on.

Market impact

Oracle feeds have worked normally throughout. As of 00:55 UTC, ETH and BTC are down about 4% since the drain. Governance tokens the exploiter holds have fallen further, with AAVE and LINK down about 9%, UNI about 8% and ARB about 6%. The freeze prevents the exploiter from depositing any of these tokens on Aave. Existing positions backed by them remain healthy, and we are watching them for liquidations as the selling continues.

Stablecoins have held their pegs. GHO slipped from about $0.998 before the drain to $0.997 as holders redeemed about 4.6M GHO for USDT through the GHO Stability Module between 21:49 and 22:07, and it has stayed near that level since.

Next steps

The situation is still developing. We will keep monitoring the exploiter’s wallets and the affected price feeds and will share updates as they come. Markets will stay frozen until the exploiter’s funds stop moving and we get more clarity on the containment from Binance’s side. We will then work with Aave Labs and the other service providers on a staged unfreeze. A long freeze also affects utilisation. Frozen reserves take no new supply, so withdrawals by large suppliers raise utilisation and borrow rates, and only repayments pull them back down. We are watching utilisation on the frozen reserves, and will evaluate the order of the unfreeze.

Between 20:58 and 21:01 UTC, one wallet in the exploiter’s cluster supplied 60M USDT on Aave V3 Ethereum Core and borrowed 19,762 WETH, worth about $44.6M at the time. This happened about 40 minutes before the first freeze at 21:42, and no exploiter wallet has interacted with Aave since 21:01. It is the exploiter’s only position on Aave across all networks and versions. The position holds $59.9M of USDT collateral against $43.8M of debt, so it is over-collateralised and remains subject to normal liquidation. It does not put Aave suppliers at risk.

What we did

Within 10 minutes of the first reports we joined Aave Labs, TokenLogic, and Certora in a joint war room. The group decided to freeze Aave markets across all networks. The exploiter could swap the stolen funds into any listed asset, so freezing only the stolen token reserves would have left other ways in. We chose a freeze because the guardian can reverse it, while cutting caps instead would have needed a governance vote and about five days to restore.

A freeze stops anyone, including the exploiter, from opening new supply or borrow positions. Users can still repay and withdraw, and liquidations keep running. Because frozen reserves take no new supply, users cannot add collateral, so while the freeze is on, repaying is the only way to raise a health factor.

Together with Aave Labs’ engineering team, we prepared and simulated the freeze transactions for every network and proposed them to the guardian multisigs, which signed and executed them between 21:42 and 23:04 UTC. In total, 175 reserves were frozen on Aave V3 across 16 networks and 117 on Aave V4 across four networks. The freeze now covers:

  • Aave V3 on the Ethereum Core and Prime markets and on Arbitrum, Avalanche, Base, BNB Chain, Celo, Gnosis, Ink, Linea, Mantle, MegaETH, Monad, Optimism, Plasma, Polygon and X Layer.
  • Aave V4 on the main Ethereum spokes, the Avalanche spokes, the Base tokenized equities spoke and the Arc spokes.

The Horizon RWA market was left open because all of its collateral is permissioned and cannot be used by the exploiter. No market has been paused.

We also track the exploiter in real time. We follow every wallet in its cluster on Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism and Avalanche, watch for any interaction with Aave, and monitor the Chainlink price feeds that Aave relies on.

Market impact

Oracle feeds have worked normally throughout. As of 00:55 UTC, ETH and BTC are down about 4% since the drain. Governance tokens the exploiter holds have fallen further, with AAVE and LINK down about 9%, UNI about 8% and ARB about 6%. The freeze prevents the exploiter from depositing any of these tokens on Aave. Existing positions backed by them remain healthy, and we are watching them for liquidations as the selling continues.

Stablecoins have held their pegs. GHO slipped from about $0.998 before the drain to $0.997 as holders redeemed about 4.6M GHO for USDT through the GHO Stability Module between 21:49 and 22:07, and it has stayed near that level since.

Next steps

The situation is still developing. We will keep monitoring the exploiter’s wallets and the affected price feeds and will share updates as they come. Markets will stay frozen until the exploiter’s funds stop moving and we get more clarity on the containment from Binance’s side. We will then work with Aave Labs and the other service providers on a staged unfreeze. A long freeze also affects utilisation. Frozen reserves take no new supply, so withdrawals by large suppliers raise utilisation and borrow rates, and only repayments pull them back down. We are watching utilisation on the frozen reserves, and will evaluate the order of the unfreeze.

governance_posts.title: Risk Stewards: Borrow and Draw Cap Reductions on Aave V3 and Aave V4 / 2026.10.30
governance_posts.description:
Summary

Following the freeze of Aave V3 and Aave V4 reserves in response to the Binance hot wallet incident on October 29, 2026, LlamaRisk recommends reducing the borrow caps of the largest Aave V3 borrow reserves and the draw caps of the largest Aave V4 credit lines to approximately 2% above the amount borrowed just before the exploit. The changes apply to Aave V3 reserves and Aave V4 spoke credit lines with more than $10M borrowed before the exploit and more than $10M of capacity left before reaching their cap.

  • Decrease borrow cap for WETH from 2,400,000 to 1,790,000.
  • Decrease borrow cap for USDT from 3,090,000,000 to 2,560,000,000.
  • Decrease borrow cap for USDC from 2,700,000,000 to 2,270,000,000.
  • Decrease borrow cap for DAI from 180,000,000 to 119,000,000.
  • Decrease borrow cap for WBTC from 1,500 to 749.
  • Decrease borrow cap for EURC from 41,400,000 to 26,600,000.
  • Decrease borrow cap for USDe from 50,000,000 to 12,400,000.
  • Decrease borrow cap for cbBTC from 500 to 149.

Aave V3 Prime:

  • Decrease borrow cap for WETH from 54,000 to 16,100.

Aave V3 Plasma:

  • Decrease borrow cap for USDT0 from 855,000,000 to 735,000,000.
  • Decrease borrow cap for USDe from 50,000,000 to 30,700,000.

Aave V3 Base:

  • Decrease borrow cap for WETH from 100,000 to 79,900.
  • Decrease borrow cap for USDC from 207,000,000 to 178,000,000.

Aave V3 Arbitrum:

  • Decrease borrow cap for USDC from 225,000,000 to 172,000,000.
  • Decrease borrow cap for WETH from 75,000 to 56,500.
  • Decrease borrow cap for USD₮0 from 112,400,000 to 39,400,000.
  • Decrease borrow cap for WBTC from 416 to 149.

  • Decrease borrow cap for WETH from 16,000 to 6,280.

Aave V3 Gnosis:

Aave V4 Ethereum:

  • Decrease the draw cap for WETH on the Core Hub EtherFi Spoke from 60K to 41.1K.
  • Decrease the draw cap for USDG on the Core Hub Main Spoke from 75M to 63.5M.
  • Decrease the draw cap for USDG on the Paxos Hub USDG Maple Spoke from 60M to 46.4M.
  • Decrease the draw cap for USDT on the Core Hub Main Spoke from 30M to 15.6M.

Aave V4 Arc:

  • Decrease the draw cap for USDC on the Core Hub Main Spoke from 100M to 69.7M.
  • Decrease the draw cap for USDC on the Core Hub USDC Maple Spoke from 60M to 41.6M.

The GHO Stewards will execute the following GHO borrow cap changes:

Aave V3 Core:

  • Decrease borrow cap for GHO from 150,000,000 to 105,000,000.

Aave V3 Prime:

  • Decrease borrow cap for GHO from 85,000,000 to 35,000,000.

Rationale

Frozen reserves accept no new supply or borrowing, so borrow and draw caps have no effect during the freeze. Once reserves are unfrozen, any unused capacity between outstanding debt and the cap becomes available at once. Before the exploit, the Aave V3 reserves in scope used between 24% and 84% of their borrow caps. The reductions remove approximately $3.7B of unused borrow capacity on Aave V3 and $130M on Aave V4. The exploiter still holds large ETH, stablecoin and governance token balances, and a reopened market with this headroom would let a single actor build a large position in the first blocks after the unfreeze.

We size each new cap from the larger of two values, the amount borrowed just before the exploit and the amount borrowed now, and add 2%. Using the larger value keeps every reserve able to return to its pre-exploit borrow size and keeps current debt below the cap. On Aave V3 Core, current WETH debt is higher than before the exploit because it includes the exploiter’s 19,762 WETH borrow, so the WETH cap is sized on current debt.

The scope is limited to the largest borrow paths, Aave V3 reserves and Aave V4 spoke credit lines with more than $10M borrowed before the exploit and more than $10M of capacity left before reaching their cap. GHO borrow caps on Aave V3 Core and Aave V3 Prime are set by the GHO Stewards. Aave V3 Horizon was not frozen and has no Risk Steward, so it is also left out. Reserves with borrowing disabled carry no new borrow capacity and need no change. Paths with less than $10M of capacity left stay unchanged.

Caps can be raised again through the regular Risk Steward process as borrow demand returns once markets are unfrozen, after the 36-hour cooldown that follows each cap update.

Frozen reserves accept no new supply or borrowing, so borrow and draw caps have no effect during the freeze. Once reserves are unfrozen, any unused capacity between outstanding debt and the cap becomes available at once. Before the exploit, the Aave V3 reserves in scope used between 24% and 84% of their borrow caps. The reductions remove approximately $3.7B of unused borrow capacity on Aave V3 and $130M on Aave V4. The exploiter still holds large ETH, stablecoin and governance token balances, and a reopened market with this headroom would let a single actor build a large position in the first blocks after the unfreeze.

We size each new cap from the larger of two values, the amount borrowed just before the exploit and the amount borrowed now, and add 2%. Using the larger value keeps every reserve able to return to its pre-exploit borrow size and keeps current debt below the cap. On Aave V3 Core, current WETH debt is higher than before the exploit because it includes the exploiter’s 19,762 WETH borrow, so the WETH cap is sized on current debt.

The scope is limited to the largest borrow paths, Aave V3 reserves and Aave V4 spoke credit lines with more than $10M borrowed before the exploit and more than $10M of capacity left before reaching their cap. GHO borrow caps on Aave V3 Core and Aave V3 Prime are set by the GHO Stewards. Aave V3 Horizon was not frozen and has no Risk Steward, so it is also left out. Reserves with borrowing disabled carry no new borrow capacity and need no change. Paths with less than $10M of capacity left stay unchanged.

Caps can be raised again through the regular Risk Steward process as borrow demand returns once markets are unfrozen, after the 36-hour cooldown that follows each cap update.

governance_posts.title: tBTC Mint & Redeem Pause: Aave's Response
governance_posts.description:
Last updated 10:26 UTC, 31 October 2026.

What happened

On 31 October 2026, Threshold Network issued a pre-emptive pause of tBTC mints & redeems. We are in communication with the Threshold team and are closely monitoring their updates.

tBTC is listed on Aave V3 on Ethereum Core, Base, and Arbitrum. The Base and Arbitrum reserves were previously frozen in earlier asset deprecation rounds, making Ethereum Core the only market where tBTC could still support new borrowing.

What we did

We recommended a pre-emptive freeze of tBTC on Aave V3 Ethereum Core. The aim is to prevent Aave’s exposure to tBTC from growing while the pause is in place by stopping new borrowing against tBTC and new tBTC deposits until the incident is confirmed to be fully mitigated by Threshold. We prepared the freeze transaction and proposed it to the guardian multisig, which executed it at 10:01 UTC.

A freeze stops new tBTC deposits and stops tBTC from adding borrowing power to any position. Users can still repay and withdraw; liquidations continue to run; and borrowing against other collateral works as normal. tBTC keeps its liquidation threshold, so the health factors of existing positions do not change and no position becomes liquidatable due to the freeze. Frozen reserves accept no new supply, so while the freeze is on, users can raise their health factor by repaying debt or adding additional collateral.

The freeze applies only to tBTC on Ethereum Core. No other reserve is affected, and no market has been paused.

Next steps

We will continue to follow Threshold’s updates and monitor tBTC positions on Aave and tBTC liquidity on secondary markets. Once we have assurance that tBTC operations return to normal, we will propose restorative measures, and we will share that update in this thread.

governance_posts.title: AL Development Update | October 2026
governance_posts.description:
Greetings, Aave community!

Aave Labs has continued to make steady progress across multiple protocol initiatives in line with its service provider scope.

During October, Aave V4 surpassed $1.5B in deposits and welcomed its first externally curated markets, while work advanced across Aave V3, integrations, technical assessments, governance, and product development. The update below reflects Aave Labs’ transparent and collaborative approach to building in public.

October update:

  • Aave reached $1.1T in all-time borrow volume.
  • Published the ARFC to establish the Aave Foundation, Phase 1.
  • Aave V4 surpassed $1.5B in deposits, reaching a new all-time high.
  • Led the integration of Sentora, the first external curator on Aave V4.
  • Onboarded syrupUSDC to Aave V4 on Arc, the first reserve to experience the Risk Premium, and USDe to Aave V4 on Avalanche.
  • Supported the Babylon integration to bring native BTC as collateral to Aave V4.
  • Published the Aave V3.8 ARFC.
  • Implemented the oracle deprecation, the Liquidation Protocol Fee increase, and the ETH and BTC collateral efficiency revision.

Aave Protocol

Aave reached $1.1T in all-time borrow volume. We also published the ARFC to establish the Aave Foundation, a memberless entity intended to hold the Aave trademark and related intellectual property for the benefit of the Aave Protocol. Phase 1 covers the incorporation of the entity and the appointment of its initial independent director and supervisor, with later phases returning to governance with their own scope.

Integrations expanded the ways businesses and builders can access Aave. Eligible Circle Mint customers can now borrow USDC against cirBTC on Arc or Ethereum, Privy Earn offers Aave yield to fintechs and neobanks, and the Aave MCP server now connects to the MetaMask Agent Wallet.

Aave V4

Aave V4 deposits crossed $1.5B, a new all-time high, while active loans surpassed $450M. On Base, the market for loans backed by tokenized stocks crossed $9M in deposits and approached $4M in loans.

Aave V4 welcomed its first externally curated markets, an integration led by our team. The proposed framework lets Sentora operate a dedicated Hub and Spokes on Ethereum, curating collateral, risk parameters, interest rate curves, and oracles. The Aave DAO retains ownership of the contracts and receives 50% of the instance revenue, while every change that increases risk passes through a 48-hour timelock. The three markets now live allow users to borrow RLUSD, PYUSD, and OUSD against yield-bearing and blue-chip collateral.

New reserves also went live. syrupUSDC from Maple was onboarded to Aave V4 on Arc, as collateral on the Maple Spoke with USDC as the borrowable asset. It is the first reserve to experience the Risk Premium, a novel feature of Aave V4 that adjusts the borrow rate based on collateral quality. USDe was onboarded to the Aave V4 Core instance on Avalanche, expanding the offering of yield-bearing assets on this instance.

The Babylon team published the ARFC to onboard native BTC as collateral on Aave V4 through Trustless Bitcoin Vaults (TBV), where BTC stays locked on the Bitcoin network without being wrapped, bridged, or held by a custodian. The integration deploys two new Spokes, the Babylon Spoke and the BTC Vault Swap Spoke, and @LlamaRisk has shared its support and risk parameter recommendations. We also supported the integration.

Aave V3

We published the ARFC to upgrade Aave V3 to V3.8, a non-invasive release focused on security. It introduces defense in depth improvements to strengthen the protocol’s security over the long term, and is released under a Business Source License with a Change Date set by Aave Governance. The release will go through audits by Certora and third parties before the AIP.

The oracle deprecation for long-tail assets proposed by @LlamaRisk was executed, with the implementation prepared by our team. Across Aave V2 and V3, it replaces Chainlink price feeds classified as high or very high risk with adapters that return a fixed price, paired with parameter changes so the remaining positions can wind down in an orderly fashion.

We also implemented two risk proposals from @LlamaRisk. The Liquidation Protocol Fee increase for WBTC, WETH, and wstETH on Aave V3 Ethereum Core was executed, raising the share of liquidation bonuses that accrues to the treasury. The revision of ETH and BTC collateral efficiency has been raised and is set for execution. It raises the loan-to-value (LTV) ratios and liquidation thresholds on Aave V3 Ethereum Core, Arbitrum, and Base, together with the collateral factors of the same assets on the Aave V4 Main Spoke.

Three Pendle Principal Tokens (PTs) were onboarded to @LlamaRisk’s PT Risk Oracle: PT-sUSDe-22OCT2026 on Aave V3 Plasma, PT-AUSD-17DEC2026 on Aave V3 Monad, and PT-USDG-25FEB2027 on Aave V3 X Layer. Their discount rate and E-Mode parameters are now maintained automatically, within bounds set by governance.

Governance Proposals

Governance work combined proposals prepared by Aave Labs with technical review for other DAO Service Providers.

We created 5 AIPs:

  • AIP 526: Oracle Deprecation for Long-tail Assets.
  • AIP 530: Move stkGHO Claim Helper Role to Updated StkGhoMigrator.
  • AIP 534: Liquidation Protocol Fee Increase for WBTC, WETH, and wstETH on Aave V3 Ethereum Core.
  • AIP 535: Onboard USDe to Aave V4 Core Instance on Avalanche.
  • AIP 536: Revision of ETH & BTC Collateral Efficiency on Aave.

The team also reviewed 8 AIPs created by DAO Service Providers:

  • AIP 524: Onboard PT-sUSDe-22OCT2026 to the LlamaRisk PT Risk Oracle.
  • AIP 525: Onboard PT-AUSD-17DEC2026 to Aave V3 Monad.
  • AIP 527: Onboard PT-AUSD-17DEC2026 to the LlamaRisk PT Risk Oracle.
  • AIP 528: Umbrella - Renew Allowances.
  • AIP 529: August/September 2026 Funding Update.
  • AIP 531: Asset Listing - Pendle PT-USDG-25FEB2027 X Layer.
  • AIP 533: Onboard USDe to Aave V3 X Layer.
  • AIP 538: Onboard PT-USDG-25FEB2027 to the LlamaRisk PT Risk Oracle.

Technical Assessments

GHO

The GHO borrow rate on Aave V3 Ethereum Core was raised from 4.25% to 4.50% annual percentage rate (APR), matching the Aave Savings Rate, and the GHO base rate on Aave V3 Ethereum Prime from 2.75% to 3.00%, through the October GHO Stewards update by @TokenLogic, which the team reviewed. We also replaced the stkGhoMigrator contract with a new version that makes migrations more resilient, with no impact on users or their funds.

The community approved the onboarding of HINC and mWIN to Aave Horizon through Snapshot votes. @LlamaRisk also raised the LTV of JAAA on Horizon from 81% to 87% and its liquidation threshold from 86% to 89% through a Risk Stewards update, based on the settlement record of the fund.

A new availability page on aave.com lists where the Aave App can be used.

  • Continue onboarding new assets to Aave V3 and Aave V4.

  • Migrate app.aave.com to the new backend.

Aave Labs has continued to make steady progress across multiple protocol initiatives in line with its service provider scope.

  • Implemented the oracle deprecation, the Liquidation Protocol Fee increase, and the ETH and BTC collateral efficiency revision.

Aave Protocol

Aave reached $1.1T in all-time borrow volume. We also published the ARFC to establish the Aave Foundation, a memberless entity intended to hold the Aave trademark and related intellectual property for the benefit of the Aave Protocol. Phase 1 covers the incorporation of the entity and the appointment of its initial independent director and supervisor, with later phases returning to governance with their own scope.

Integrations expanded the ways businesses and builders can access Aave. Eligible Circle Mint customers can now borrow USDC against cirBTC on Arc or Ethereum, Privy Earn offers Aave yield to fintechs and neobanks, and the Aave MCP server now connects to the MetaMask Agent Wallet.

Aave V4

Aave V4 deposits crossed $1.5B, a new all-time high, while active loans surpassed $450M. On Base, the market for loans backed by tokenized stocks crossed $9M in deposits and approached $4M in loans.

Aave V4 welcomed its first externally curated markets, an integration led by our team. governance_posts.title: Risk Stewards: Supply and Borrow Cap Increases on Aave V3 / 2026.11.02
governance_posts.description:
Summary

LlamaRisk recommends the following parameter changes based on user behavior, on-chain liquidity, and position health observed in the latest review of Aave V3 reserves.

Aave V3 X Layer:

  • Increase supply cap for USDe from 25,000,000 to 50,000,000.

Aave V3 Monad:

  • Increase borrow cap for USDT0 from 57,900,000 to 63,000,000.

Aave V3 Optimism:

  • Increase borrow cap for WETH from 6,280 to 7,750.

USDe (Aave V3 X Layer)

USDe sits at 45.8% supply cap utilization on the Aave V3 X Layer instance as of November 2, 2026, with supply up from approximately 2.8M on October 29, 2026. The reserve carries no outstanding debt against its 10M borrow cap and acts as collateral only inside the USDe Stablecoins E-Mode (LTV 91.00%, LT 93.00%).

USDe Supply Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, November 2, 2026

Supply is concentrated, with the largest supplier holding approximately 76% and the top three approximately 98%. Four of the top five suppliers carry debt at HF between 1.02 and 1.03, borrowing USD₮0, USDC, and USDG against USDe, and since USDe is priced via the USDT/USD feed, the liquidation risk of these positions is low.

Recommendation

We recommend raising the supply cap from 25,000,000 to 50,000,000 on Aave V3 X Layer, landing at approximately 22.9% post-change cap utilization.

USDT0 (Aave V3 Monad)

USDT0 sits at 100.0% borrow cap utilization (57,902,769 / 57,900,000) on the Aave V3 Monad instance as of November 2, 2026. At current supply, the proposed cap corresponds to 97.0% reserve utilization, above the 92.00% optimal point.

USDT0 Borrow Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, November 2, 2026

Debt is concentrated, with the largest borrower holding approximately 26% and the top three approximately 57%, and the borrowers shown run HF between 1.02 and 2.44 with a median of 1.04. Their debt is denominated in stablecoins, with eight posting syrupUSDC and four each posting USDe and PT-AUSD-17DEC2026 as collateral.

Recommendation

We recommend raising the borrow cap from 57,900,000 to 63,000,000 on Aave V3 Monad, landing at approximately 91.9% post-change cap utilization.

WETH (Aave V3 Optimism)

WETH sits at 98.5% borrow cap utilization (6,185 / 6,280) on the Aave V3 Optimism instance as of November 2, 2026. At current supply, the proposed cap corresponds to 90.2% reserve utilization, above the 90.00% optimal point.

WETH Borrow Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, November 2, 2026

All of the top twenty borrowers post wstETH as their only collateral at HF between 1.01 and 1.39 with a median of 1.04, holding approximately 91% of debt, with the largest holding approximately 28% and the top three approximately 51%. HF for the cohort depends on the wstETH/ETH exchange rate.

Recommendation

We recommend raising the borrow cap from 6,280 to 7,750 on Aave V3 Optimism, landing at approximately 79.8% post-change cap utilization.

Specification

Supply Caps

Aave V3 X Layer USDe 25,000,000 50,000,000

Aave V3 Optimism WETH 6,280 7,750

Next Steps

We will move forward and implement these updates via the Risk Steward process. The implemented changes can be reviewed on the LlamaRisk Risk Stewards Dashboard.

Summary

LlamaRisk recommends the following parameter changes based on user behavior, on-chain liquidity, and position health observed in the latest review of Aave V3 reserves.

Aave V3 X Layer:

  • Increase borrow cap for USD₮0 from 35,000,000 to 70,000,000.

Aave V3 Avalanche:

  • Reduce supply cap for WAVAX from 14,000,000 to 12,000,000.

USD₮0 (Aave V3 X Layer)

USD₮0 sits at 72.5% borrow cap utilization (25,380,870 / 35,000,000) on the Aave V3 X Layer instance as of November 3, 2026. The proposed cap exceeds the supplied balance, so available liquidity becomes the limit on new borrowing, and withdrawals beyond that amount may depend on repayment or new supply.

USD₮0 Borrow Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, November 3, 2026

The top twenty borrowers hold approximately 83% of debt at HF between 1.03 and 1.10 with a median of 1.05. The largest borrower holds approximately 31% of debt against USDe collateral and the top three approximately 47%, while eighteen of the twenty post PT-USDG-25FEB2027 as collateral, so HF for most of the cohort depends on the PT price.

Recommendation

We recommend raising the borrow cap from 35,000,000 to 70,000,000 on Aave V3 X Layer, landing at approximately 36.3% post-change cap utilization.

Cap Reductions

WAVAX on Aave V3 Avalanche sits at 115.9% supply cap utilization (16,229,566 / 14,000,000) as of November 3, 2026, with some users migrating their WAVAX supply to Aave V4. The proposed cap of 12,000,000 sits below current outstanding supply (approximately 135.2% post-change cap utilization), which keeps new supply blocked until supply falls below the new cap, preventing WAVAX exposure on this instance from rebuilding as those positions move.
